author: beehive state news
title: No. 24 BYU secures spot in National Championship with fourth-place finish at NCAA Athens Regional
text:
The Brigham Young University men’s golf team earned a place in the NCAA National Championship after finishing fourth at the NCAA Athens Regional on May 20 at the University of Georgia Golf Club.
The result allows BYU to advance to the national finals, an achievement that marks their 34th appearance at this stage. The team’s strong performance was highlighted by a final round score of nine under par, bringing their overall total to twenty under par for the event.
Head coach Bruce Brockbank said, “I’m so excited for our team. This is about them. They played some outstanding golf this week. I love going to the NCAA finals.” Director of golf Todd Miller added, “I think more than anything what kept running through my mind is we need to get back to the national championship for Bruce’s final year. The guys had a good bounce in their step from the first shot, and I feel like they stayed really present all day long.”
Freshman Parker Bunn tied for tenth place individually with a six-under-par total and recorded his first top-10 finish in his initial regional appearance. Miller said, “It was an incredible performance by Parker stepping into that fifth spot on our team and really carrying us this week.” Brockbank also said, “Parker Bunn was our MVP.” Kihei Akina finished tied for fourteenth at five under par in his first regional tournament and achieved his eleventh career top-15 placement out of thirteen tournaments.
Other notable performances included Peter Kim’s three-under-par finish inside the top twenty-five and Simon Kwon’s six-under-par final round that helped secure BYU’s advancement. Miller said about Kwon’s play, “Simon had a tough tournament overall, but it was a special round for him today, hitting a lot of shots and making putts. He’ll remember that for many years.” Tyson Shelley concluded his last regional event tied for forty-second place at one over par.
Looking ahead, BYU will travel to Carlsbad, California to compete in the NCAA National Championship from May 29 through June 3 at Omni La Costa Resort.
